glosses: to orphan (to die, making (one's child) an orphan)

examples.text: Kilka miesięcy temu skarciłem kobietę w pewnej parafii, bo była w ciąży z ósmym dzieckiem, po siedmiu porodach cesarskich: „Czy chce pani osierocić siedmioro dzieci?".
examples.translation: A few months ago I rebuked a woman in a certain parish because she was pregnant with an eighth child after seven Caesarean sections: "Do you want to leave seven children as orphans?"
examples.english: A few months ago I rebuked a woman in a certain parish because she was pregnant with an eighth child after seven Caesarean sections: "Do you want to leave seven children as orphans?"

glosses: to orphan, to abandon, to leave

examples.text:
Kraku, dzielności tej nie życzę tobie,
Ona cię zgubi i kraj osieroci.
examples.translation:
Krak, I do not wish you had such bravery:
It will leave you lost and the country abandoned.
examples.english:

examples.translation: The Czechs have a chance to leave [the] Visegrad [alliance].

opuściwszy jakieś miejsce, sprawić, że popadło w ruinę
A person, especially a minor, both or (rarely) one of whose parents have died.

examples.text: Rudolf was the bold, bad Baron of traditional melodrama. Irene was young, as pretty as a picture, fresh from a music academy in England. He was the scion of an ancient noble family; she an orphan without money or friends.

glosses: A person, especially a minor, whose parents have permanently abandoned them.
A young animal with no mother.
Anything that is unsupported, as by its source, provider or caretaker, by reason of the supporter's demise or decision to abandon.
A single line of type, beginning a paragraph, at the bottom of a column or page.

examples.text: An orphan isn't harmful in a language that has garbage collection, such as Java. However, reducing the number of orphans can be expected to improve code performance.

glosses: Remaining after the removal of some form of support.

examples.text: With its government funding curtailed, the gun registry became an orphan program.

glosses: To deprive of parents (used almost exclusively in the passive).

examples.text: What do you do when you come across two orphaned polar bear cubs?

glosses: To make unavailable, as by removing the last remaining pointer or reference to.

examples.text: Removing categories orphans pages from the main category tree.
When you removed that image tag, you orphaned the resized icon.

glosses: сделать сиротою, лишить отца или матери, либо обоих

examples.text: С нас головы посымают, детей осиротят!
В лесу тихо; кроме овсянок, ничего, только в глубине леса, на скате, встретил парочку кукш и осиротил одну из них.
— Попадья моя, Марья Митревна, осиротила меня ещё в молодых годах.
